name: Summarise weekly competitor news from Bounce Watch with OpenAI to email

parameters.content:
## Summarise weekly competitor news from Bounce Watch with OpenAI to email

Bounce Watch tells you what just happened at a company and when — funding, senior hires, new offices, customer wins and partnerships, each carrying its own date. What the API covers: bouncewatch.com/products/data-enrichment-api

Watching three or four competitors by hand means opening a lot of tabs and reading a lot of nothing. This workflow pulls each of their timelines once a week, has OpenAI write the digest, and emails it to you.

### How it works

A Monday schedule starts the run. A Settings node holds the competitor domains as a list, and a split node turns that list into one item per company. Each one goes to Bounce Watch for its dated timeline. An aggregate node gathers every timeline into a single item, and OpenAI writes the digest from it. The prompt is explicit about the two things a summary usually gets wrong: dates that record when a change was measured are not claims about when it happened, and an empty timeline is not evidence that a company was quiet.

### Setup

1. Get an API key at bouncewatch.com/register/api. It is free, no card, and every new account starts with 2,500 credits. Paste it into the Bounce Watch credential.
2. Put your competitor domains into Competitor list.
3. Connect your OpenAI credential and pick a model.
4. Fill in the From and To addresses on the email node and pick your SMTP credential.

### Customization tips

Narrow each timeline with signal keys or categories if you only care about product launches or hiring. Send the digest to Slack instead by swapping the last node.

Split turns the list into one item each.

## Pull each timeline

## Summarise and send

The prompt states the rules about dates

values.content: You are writing a short weekly competitor digest for a founder. Rules you must follow. A date marked date_is_measurement is the date the change was recorded, not the date it happened — print it as a plain date and never write that the company did something on that date. A signal marked unconfirmed is inference, not announcement; say so or leave it out. A competitor with no signals in the window has not been shown to be quiet — say that nothing matched this week, never that the company has been inactive. Do not invent numbers, amounts or headcounts that are not in the input. Keep it to a few lines per competitor, plain text, no preamble.

={{ $json.data.map(c => (c.company?.name || c.company?.domain) + " (" + (c.company?.domain || "") + ")
" + ((c.signals || []).length ? c.signals.map(s => "- [" + s.date + "]" + (s.date_is_measurement ? " (date recorded)" : "") + " " + s.label + (s.unconfirmed ? " (unconfirmed)" : "") + (s.summary ? ": " + s.summary : "")).join("
") : "- nothing matched this window")).join("

") }}
